questions.q: A project manager who works in a national bank decides to use the power/interest grid to plan stakeholder engagement. How should he deal with an interested stakeholder with little authority? *
questions.e: The power/interest grid suggests that stakeholders with high interest but low power should be kept informed since they are engaged and can influence the project indirectly.

questions.q: A project manager is leading an agricultural project involving three stakeholders with high authority. By analyzing each of these stakeholders, the project manager identifies Stakeholder A as the one who has the most interest in the project. What strategy should the project manager use for managing Stakeholder A? *
questions.e: Stakeholders with high power and high interest should be managed closely to ensure their expectations are met and they remain supportive of the project.

questions.q: A project manager works for Massive Fun, a company specializing in eco-friendly kids’ toys. Two months into the project, they launch the second phase consisting in developing biodegradable playing dough. Hence, the project manager meets with the sponsor to check if any potential players were left out in the first phase and to discuss these new stakeholders’ influence. The activity that the project manager is carrying out with the sponsor can be identified as: *
questions.e: Identifying stakeholders involves recognizing new stakeholders and understanding their influence on the project.

questions.q: You are managing a project to develop a new mobile application for a financial services company. A key stakeholder, the Chief Technology Officer (CTO), is highly influential but has expressed concerns about the project's security measures. The CTO has a high level of power in the organization but does not seem actively involved in the day-to-day activities of the project. How should you manage this stakeholder? *
questions.e: Since the CTO has high power but a lower level of involvement in the project, the best approach is to keep them satisfied. Stakeholders with high power but low interest should be managed by ensuring that their concerns are addressed while not overwhelming them with too much engagement. This approach helps maintain their support without requiring excessive involvement in project details.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to an eco-friendly packaging project. In order to manage involved stakeholders, the project manager starts by analyzing their power, urgency, and legitimacy. Which analysis method is the project manager applying? *
questions.e: The salience model considers power, urgency, and legitimacy to prioritize stakeholders effectively.

questions.q: When the execution of a rebranding project was completed, several key stakeholders, including the sponsor, were reluctant to accept deliverables and close the project. What should the project manager do in this situation? (Select three) *

o.t: Identify and resolve any open issues. Then, be firm on formal closure.
Formally close the project. Stakeholders will get well-acquainted with the new brand by that time.
Identify and openly discuss the reasons for reluctance.
Invite earnest feedback from all sides and try to identify any misunderstanding.

questions.e: Identifying and resolving any open issues ensures that all stakeholder concerns are addressed, which is crucial for gaining their acceptance of the deliverables. Openly discussing the reasons for reluctance helps understand stakeholder concerns and provides an opportunity to address them, fostering better communication and trust. Inviting earnest feedback from all sides and identifying any misunderstandings can help clarify issues and ensure that stakeholders feel heard and their concerns are properly managed before proceeding to formal project closure.

questions.q: A project manager for Steel Foundations has been brought on to the project in the very early stages and has been asked to write its charter. Over the past week, the project manager met with a number of stakeholders, received their input, and is now ready to have the charter signed. Who is responsible for signing the project charter? *
questions.e: The project sponsor authorizes the project by signing the project charter.

questions.q: A project manager was assigned to a park redevelopment project which consists of cleaning and equipping the park for local families and residents. The project involves a really big number of stakeholders since it includes multiple phases and different types of tasks to execute. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Analyze all stakeholders in order to prioritize engagement
Report the issue to the project sponsor

questions.e: The project manager should analyze all stakeholders to understand their power, interest, and influence. This analysis helps in prioritizing engagement and ensuring that the needs and expectations of the most influential and interested stakeholders are addressed appropriately. Ignoring any group of stakeholders could lead to overlooking critical inputs and potential risks.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to lead a recycling project. During the project planning phase, the defined scope was approved by management and all stakeholders. During the execution of the project work, two key stakeholders ask the project manager to change a particular part of the scope statement. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the stakeholders to submit a change request
Refuse to alter the scope since it has already been approved by all stakeholders
Refuse to alter the scope since it cannot be modified after being officially approved
Refer the stakeholders to the project sponsor

questions.e: The proper procedure for handling changes to the project scope is through the change request process. This ensures that any proposed changes are documented, evaluated for impacts on the project, and approved or rejected in an organized manner, maintaining project control and alignment with stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: You are a project manager for a digital transformation project in a logistics company. During stakeholder analysis, you identify a senior executive who has high power and high interest in the project. However, this executive constantly expresses concerns and seems skeptical about the project’s success. What is the best strategy to manage this stakeholder? *
questions.e: Stakeholders with high power and high interest should be managed closely because they have significant influence over the success of the project. Since this executive expresses concerns and appears skeptical, it is essential to establish regular communication, address their worries, and ensure they remain positively engaged. Proactively managing this stakeholder can help prevent resistance and improve alignment with project objectives.

questions.q: You are identifying stakeholders at the beginning of your project. You need to classify them in order to perform stakeholder analysis. You grouped the stakeholders based on their active involvement in the project and their ability to effect changes to the project's planning or execution. Which classification model did you use? *
questions.e: The impact/influence grid classifies stakeholders based on their ability to affect the project.

questions.q: Which of the following can be a result of not engaging stakeholders effectively? *
questions.e: Ineffective stakeholder engagement can lead to misunderstandings, unmet requirements, and dissatisfaction, which may ultimately result in issues such as product recalls due to defects or non-compliance with stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: A new organization has implemented few projects and outcomes were successfully delivered to the customers. The organization's PMO wants to evaluate the degree of customers' satisfaction with the products and the projects and whether those customers are willing to recommend a product or service to others. Which of the following metrics can they use? *
questions.e: Net Promoter Score (NPS) is a metric used to measure customer satisfaction and loyalty by asking customers how likely they are to recommend a product or service to others. It helps organizations gauge the overall customer sentiment and predict business growth.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes how stakeholders are involved in a project? *

o.t: They help to determine project constraints and product deliverables.
They help determine the project deliverables and project schedule.
They help to provide project assumptions and determine the resources needs in the project.
They create the project management plan and approve the project charter.

questions.e: Stakeholders play a crucial role in providing input on project constraints (such as time, cost, and scope) and in defining the product deliverables, ensuring the project meets their needs and expectations.

questions.q: Jana is a CFO who is very busy. Her signature is required on all project documents. How would you manage Jana? *
questions.e: As a high-level stakeholder with significant influence, Jana should be managed closely to ensure her needs are met and to secure her support. The "Satisfy" strategy involves keeping her informed and engaged enough to ensure her approval and support for project documents.

questions.q: A sales manager is overpromising deliverables beyond the contractual scope. In order to resolve the disagreement, the project manager wishes to find someone with a higher ranking in the sales department who is favorable to the project. What project data should the project manager consult? *
questions.e: The stakeholder power/interest grid helps identify stakeholders with the most influence (power) and interest in the project. By consulting this grid, the project manager can identify a higher-ranking stakeholder in the sales department who can help resolve the issue.

questions.q: During a weekly project status meeting, you ask one of the stakeholders if he reviewed the document you sent him last week. He said "I'm not sure, I don't know what you are talking about". Which engagement level is this stakeholder displaying? *
questions.e: The stakeholder's response indicates a lack of awareness about the project activities and documentation, which aligns with the "Unaware" engagement level.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes when stakeholders identification is performed during the project? *

o.t: At the beginning of the project.
Only when a new stakeholder is discovered.
Before starting to prepare the project management plan.

questions.e: Stakeholder identification is an ongoing process that occurs throughout the project lifecycle. New stakeholders may be identified, and their influence or impact may change, requiring continuous engagement and management.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a project with internal stakeholders only and was warned by the project sponsor that some stakeholders require special attention. The organization is very hierarchical. Which of the following models should be used in this instance? *
questions.e: The power-influence grid is useful in hierarchical organizations to assess authority and impact.

questions.q: A project manager learns that they were not assigned the human resources they were promised during the planning phase. Instead, they got a team that did not have the required skills for executing the project work. Taking into consideration that they work in a weak matrix organization, what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Issue a change request to get a more qualified team
Negotiate with the functional manager in order to obtain the required team members
Take the matter to the project sponsor
Use their legitimate power by informing the organization that they will not perform the project without the needed resources

questions.e: In a weak matrix organization, the functional manager has more authority over resources. The project manager should negotiate with the functional manager to obtain the required team members with the necessary skills.

questions.q: A project manager conducted an analysis with relevant stakeholders and identified multiple conflicts regarding the expected project benefits. Which action should the project manager take first? *

o.t: Formal approval of project change requests is required before benefits realization is updated.
Stakeholder dissatisfaction with key project deliverables should be addressed through the change management process.
Conflict in subsequent phases of the project may arise due to inconsistent stakeholder expectations.
Inconsistent input on benefits from key stakeholders should be resolved through structured stakeholder engagement strategies.

questions.e: The best approach to resolve conflicts regarding project benefits is to engage stakeholders in a structured manner and address inconsistencies in expectations. A structured stakeholder engagement strategy ensures alignment on project objectives and expected benefits.

questions.q: While gathering requirements for the project scope, the project manager identifies significant disagreements among key stakeholders. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Assist affected stakeholders in reaching a consensus through facilitation techniques.
Follow the recommendation of the technical consultant to proceed with the most viable option.
Escalate to the project sponsor to make a decision on behalf of the stakeholders.
Conduct a meeting with the disagreeing parties to determine the best course of action.

questions.e: The project manager should facilitate discussions among stakeholders to help them reach a consensus rather than making unilateral decisions or escalating too soon. Facilitation techniques help stakeholders align their expectations and avoid future conflicts.

questions.q: A stakeholder complains that a product component does not meet their expectations. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Check if the component meets the design and performance specifications.
Collaborate with the stakeholder to confirm their expectations.
Ask a user experience expert to meet with the stakeholder.
Raise a change request according to the stakeholder's requirements.

questions.e: Verifying the component against specifications ensures that the product meets agreed-upon requirements before considering changes.

questions.q: During project execution, a key stakeholder is replaced by a new individual. The new stakeholder has different expectations and is requesting changes. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Organize a meeting with the sponsor before the new stakeholder makes changes.
Update the stakeholder register to include the new stakeholder's expectations and engagement strategy.
Ask the previous stakeholder to hold a meeting with the new stakeholder.
Update the project charter during the execution phase to accommodate the new stakeholder’s requests.

questions.e: Updating the stakeholder register ensures the project manager formally acknowledges the new stakeholder's influence and engagement level. Changes should not be made arbitrarily without following the change management process.

questions.q: A project manager conducted an analysis with relevant stakeholders to validate project alignment with organizational strategy and expected business value. Several key stakeholders missed the analysis session, and their input was not included in the analysis. What is the main consequence of stakeholders missing the analysis session? *

o.t: Formal approval of project change requests is delayed.
Stakeholder dissatisfaction with key project deliverables.
Conflict in subsequent phases of the project may result.
Inconsistent input on benefits from key stakeholders.

questions.e: Inconsistent input on benefits from key stakeholders can lead to ambiguity and misalignment between project goals and stakeholder expectations. If all relevant stakeholders do not participate in key discussions, their perspectives may not be fully considered, impacting project outcomes.
